=== Bidder's Choice: Sealed Pool ===

SETUP. There are 3 to 5 players. Every player starts with 20 coins and no objects. The pool holds six objects: A, B, C, D, E, F. Each player privately receives the six values 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 14, one value per object, in an independent random order for each player. Every player's values therefore total 44. A player sees only his own values.

ROUNDS. The game lasts exactly 6 rounds. Each round:
1) ANNOUNCE. The round number, the objects still in the pool, every player's coins and every player's holdings are shown to all.
2) TALK. Every player writes one message of at most 40 words at the same time, without seeing the others. Any words beyond the 40th are dropped. Then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
3) BID. Every player at the same time submits a sealed bid: a whole number from 0 up to his current coins. A bid that is missing, not a whole number, negative, or above his current coins counts as 0.
4) WINNER. The highest bid wins. If several players share the highest bid, the one among them holding the fewest objects wins. If several of those also hold equally few objects, there is NO SALE this round: nobody pays, no object leaves the pool, and the round still counts as played.
5) PAY AND PICK. If there is a winner, he pays his bid, so his coins decrease by his bid. He then names one object still in the pool. That object leaves the pool and is added to his holdings. If he names no object still in the pool, or gives no answer, he receives instead the remaining object with the highest of his own values (ties: earliest letter). A player may win any number of rounds.
6) REVEAL. All bids, the winner (or 'no sale') and the object taken are announced to all.

END. After round 6, any objects still in the pool are discarded. Each player's final score = his remaining coins + the sum of HIS OWN values for the objects he holds. All values are then revealed. The player with the highest final score wins. If two or more players share the highest final score, they share the result (a draw among them).

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Bidder's Choice: Sealed Pool ===

SETUP. There are 3 to 5 players. Every player starts with 20 coins and no objects. The pool holds six objects: A, B, C, D, E, F. Each player privately receives the six values 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 14, one value per object, in an independent random order for each player. Every player's values therefore total 44. A player sees only his own values.

ROUNDS. The game lasts exactly 6 rounds. Each round:
1) ANNOUNCE. The round number, the objects still in the pool, every player's coins and every player's holdings are shown to all.
2) TALK. Every player writes one message of at most 40 words at the same time, without seeing the others. Any words beyond the 40th are dropped. Then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
3) BID. Every player at the same time submits a sealed bid: a whole number from 0 up to his current coins. A bid that is missing, not a whole number, negative, or above his current coins counts as 0.
4) WINNER. The highest bid wins. If several players share the highest bid, the one among them holding the fewest objects wins. If several of those also hold equally few objects, there is NO SALE this round: nobody pays, no object leaves the pool, and the round still counts as played.
5) PAY AND PICK. If there is a winner, he pays his bid, so his coins decrease by his bid. He then names one object still in the pool. That object leaves the pool and is added to his holdings. If he names no object still in the pool, or gives no answer, he receives instead the remaining object with the highest of his own values (ties: earliest letter). A player may win any number of rounds.
6) REVEAL. All bids, the winner (or 'no sale') and the object taken are announced to all.

END. After round 6, any objects still in the pool are discarded. Each player's final score = his remaining coins + the sum of HIS OWN values for the objects he holds. All values are then revealed. The player with the highest final score wins. If two or more players share the highest final score, they share the result (a draw among them).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 3. Seats are numbered 1 to 3.
You are seat 3, Curie. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

You start with: You are seat 3. coins 20, holdings [], value_a 10, value_b 8, value_c 6, value_d 4, value_e 2, value_f 14. you know seat 1 coins 20, holdings []; seat 2 coins 20, holdings []. max_players 5, min_bid 0, min_players 3, object_count 6, pool ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F'], round 0, rounds 6, starting_coins 20, suggested_players 3, taken_object , talk_max_words 40, tiebreak_key_multiplier 10, value_1 2, value_2 4, value_3 6, value_4 8, value_5 10, value_6 14, value_total 44, winner_seat 0. still playing: 1, 2, 3.

Each round runs in this order: a new round → the announcement → talk → sealed bid → find the winner → the winner pays → pick an object → the object changes hands → the reveal → the reveal, no sale → final scoring → values revealed → after the last round.

Actions you may be asked for:
  talk         answer with what you want to say
  sealed_bid   answer with a whole number, in the range you are given
  pick_an_object answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.
